note: Hand-written questions. The generator never writes this file; see scripts/build_question_bank.py for how authored and generated items are merged.

items.prompt: A pattern is made with sticks. Figure 1 uses 4 sticks and each new figure uses 3 more sticks than the one before. Describe figure 4 and say how many sticks it uses.
A pupil predicts that figure 10 of the stick pattern above uses 31 sticks. Use the rule to check whether the prediction is right.
items.answer: 4 + 9 x 3 = 31, so the prediction is right.

items.prompt: A pattern of tiles grows as 2, 5, 8, 11 ... Draw or describe the fifth figure and say how many tiles it has.
items.answer: Each figure adds 3 tiles, so the fifth figure has 11 + 3 = 14 tiles.

items.prompt: You want to find out which of four sports pupils in your school like best. Write the question you would put in a questionnaire.
items.answer: For example: Which of these sports do you like best? Football / Athletics / Volleyball / Table tennis. Tick one.

items.prompt: Write two things a questionnaire question should not do.
items.answer: It should not ask two questions at once, and it should not lead the reader to one answer.

items.prompt: You have collected the answers to your questionnaire from 40 pupils. Say how you would record the answers and which graph you would use to present them, and why.
items.answer: Record them in a tally chart or a table, then use a bar graph: the sports are separate groups, so the bars show how many pupils chose each one.
